Within several months he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, retaining his commissioner and academician posts as before. The inner eunuch Ju Wenjing hated his manipulation of power and stripped him of his academician post. When the edict was issued Shuwen was greatly alarmed and told others, "I, Shuwen, must at times come here to discuss official business; without this post there is no way to enter the inner palace." Wang Pi pleaded on his behalf, and he was permitted to enter the Hanlin Academy once every three or five days; in the end his inner post was cut. When Shuwen first entered the inner court he secretly shaped confidential orders, his designs invisible; he then broadcast judgments on promotion and demotion. People had not yet discerned his root and believed him a rare talent. Once he held the profit lever of the two commissions and stood among the outer court, wise and foolish alike said, "The fox in the city wall and the ghost in the mountain must by night cry from their dens to bring fortune or disaster upon people—thus they are deemed supernatural and feared; but once they run out by day, they are surely powerless."
39
叔文在省署，不復舉其職事，引其黨與竊語，謀奪內官兵柄，乃以故將範希朝統京西北諸鎮行營兵馬使，韓泰副之。 初，中人尚未悟，會邊上諸將各以狀辭中尉，且言方屬希朝，中人始悟兵柄為叔文所奪，中尉乃止諸鎮無以兵馬入。 希朝、韓泰已至奉天，諸將不至，乃還。 無幾，叔文母死。 前一日，叔文置酒饌於翰林院，宴諸學士及內官李忠言、俱文珍、劉光奇等。 中飲，叔文白諸人曰：「叔文母疾病，比來盡心戮力為國家事，不避好惡難易者，欲以報聖人之重知也。 若一去此職，百謗斯至，誰肯助叔文一言者，望諸君開懷見察。」 又曰：「羊士諤非毀叔文，欲杖殺之，而韋執誼懦不遂。 叔文生平不識劉闢，乃以韋臯意求領三川，辟排門相幹，欲執叔文手，豈非兇人耶！ 叔文已令掃木場，將斬之，韋執誼苦執不可。」 叔文無以對。
Shuwen in the ministry offices no longer performed his duties but gathered his faction for whispered counsel, plotting to seize control of the inner palace army; he therefore appointed the former general Fan Xichao overall commander of the field armies of the northwest capital commands, with Han Tai as his deputy. At first the eunuchs had not yet understood; then frontier generals each sent memorials declining the chief eunuch and saying they were now under Xichao's command; the eunuchs then realized military power had been seized by Shuwen, and the chief eunuch thereupon forbade the various commands to bring troops in. Xichao and Han Tai had already reached Fengtian, but the generals did not come; they then returned. Before long Shuwen's mother died. The day before, Shuwen set out food and drink in the Hanlin Academy and feasted the academicians and the inner eunuchs Li Zhongyan, Ju Wenjing, and Liu Guangqi. Mid-feast Shuwen addressed the assembly, saying, "My mother is ill. Lately I have devoted myself wholeheartedly to affairs of state, not shunning what is agreeable or difficult, wishing to repay the sage emperor's great trust. If I leave this post, a hundred slanders will at once arise—who will speak a word in my defense? I hope you gentlemen will open your hearts and understand." He also said, "Yang Shiyu did not slander me; I wished to have him beaten to death, but Wei Zhiyi was cowardly and would not carry it out. In life I never knew Liu Bi, yet at Wei Gao's request he sought to take command of the Three Rivers; Bi pushed through the gate to interfere and wished to seize my hand—is he not a violent man! I had already ordered the timber yard cleared to behead him, but Wei Zhiyi bitterly held fast and would not permit it." Shuwen had no reply.
40
叔文未欲立皇太子。 順宗既久疾未平，群臣中外請立太子，既而詔下立廣陵王為太子，天下皆悅； 叔文獨有憂色，而不敢言其事，但吟杜甫題諸葛亮祠堂詩末句云：「出師未捷身先死，長使英雄淚滿襟。」 因歔欷泣下，人皆竊笑之。 皇太子監國，貶為渝州司戶，明年誅之。
Shuwen did not yet wish to establish a crown prince. Shunzong had long been ill without recovery; court and countryside alike petitioned to establish a crown prince; soon an edict was issued establishing the Prince of Guangling as crown prince, and all under heaven rejoiced. Only Shuwen wore a troubled look and dared not speak of the matter; he merely recited the closing line of Du Fu's poem on Zhuge Liang's shrine, "He marched forth before victory was won, and died—forever leaving heroes with tears soaking their collars." He then sighed and wept; people all secretly laughed at him. When the crown prince supervised the state he was demoted to registrar of Yu Prefecture; the following year he was executed.
41
王伾，杭州人。 始為翰林侍書待詔，累遷至正議大夫、殿中丞、皇太子侍書。 順宗即位，遷左散騎常侍，依前翰林待詔。
Wang Pi was a native of Hangzhou. He began as Hanlin attendant scribe awaiting summons; he was promoted successively to Regular Grand Master, Palace Aide, and tutor scribe to the crown prince. When Shunzong took the throne he was promoted to Left Regular Attendant, retaining his former post as Hanlin attendant awaiting summons.
42
伾阘茸，不如叔文，唯招賄賂，無大志，貌寢陋，吳語，素為太子之所褻狎； 而叔文頗任氣自許，粗知書，好言事，順宗稍敬之，不得如伾出入無間。 叔文入止翰林，而伾入至柿林院，見李忠言、牛昭容等。 然各有所主：伾主往來傳授； 王叔文主決斷； 韋執誼為文誥； 劉禹錫、陳諫、韓曄、韓泰、柳宗元、房啟、淩準等謀議唱和，采聽外事。 而伾與叔文及諸朋黨之門，車馬填湊，而伾門尤盛，珍玩賂遺，歲時不絕。 室中為無門大櫃，唯開一竅，足以受物，以藏金寶，其妻或寢臥於上。 與叔文同貶開州司馬。
Pi was crude and unimpressive compared with Shuwen; he did nothing but solicit bribes and had no great ambitions. He was homely and ugly, spoke the Wu dialect, and had long been on familiar terms with the crown prince; Shuwen, by contrast, was headstrong and self-assured, knew books in a rough way, and liked to talk politics. Emperor Shunzong respected him somewhat, yet he could not come and go as freely as Pi. When Shuwen entered the palace he stopped at the Hanlin Academy, while Pi went on to the Persimmon Grove Academy to see Li Zhongyan, Niu Zhaorong, and others. Yet each had his role: Pi handled communication back and forth; Wang Shuwen made the decisions; Wei Zhiyi drafted official documents; Liu Yuxi, Chen Jian, Han Ye, Han Tai, Liu Zongyuan, Fang Qi, Ling Zhun, and others plotted together, advising and gathering intelligence on outside affairs. The gates of Pi, Shuwen, and their faction were jammed with carriages and horses, Pi's gate most of all; precious gifts poured in without cease through the seasons. In his room stood a doorless great cabinet with only a single opening large enough to pass things through, where he stored gold and jewels; his wife sometimes slept on top of it. He was banished together with Shuwen to serve as aide to the prefect of Kai Prefecture.
43
王叔文最所重者，李景儉、呂溫。 叔文用事時，景儉居喪於東都； 呂溫使吐蕃，留半歲，叔文敗方歸。 陸質為皇太子侍讀，尋卒。
Those Wang Shuwen valued most were Li Jingjian and Lü Wen. While Shuwen held power, Jingjian was in mourning at the Eastern Capital; Lü Wen was on a mission to Tibet and remained half a year, returning only after Shuwen's downfall. Lu Zhi served as tutor to the crown prince and soon died.
44
伾、叔文既逐，詔貶其黨韓曄饒州司馬，韓泰虔州司馬，陳諫臺州司馬，柳宗元永州司馬，劉禹錫朗州司馬，淩準連州司馬，程异郴州司馬，韋執誼崖州司馬。
After Pi and Shuwen were expelled, an edict banished their faction: Han Ye as aide to the prefect of Rao, Han Tai as aide to Qian, Chen Jian as aide to Tai, Liu Zongyuan as aide to Yong, Liu Yuxi as aide to Lang, Ling Zhun as aide to Lian, Cheng Yi as aide to Chen, and Wei Zhiyi as aide to Ya.
45
韓曄，宰相滉之族子，有俊才，依附韋執誼，累遷尚書司封郎中。 叔文敗，貶池州刺史，尋改饒州司馬，量移汀州刺史，又轉永州卒。
Han Ye was a clansman of Chancellor Han Huang's family; gifted and ambitious, he attached himself to Wei Zhiyi and rose to Director of the Department of Enfeoffment in the Ministry of Rites. After Shuwen's fall he was demoted to prefect of Chi, soon reassigned as aide of Rao, transferred by measure to prefect of Ting, then moved again to Yong, where he died.
46
陳諫至叔文敗，已出為河中少尹，自臺州司馬量移封州刺史，轉通州卒。
By the time Chen Jian fell with Shuwen he had already left office as vice governor of Hezhong; from aide of Tai he was transferred by measure to prefect of Feng, then moved to Tong, where he died.
47
淩準，貞元二十年自浙東觀察判官、侍御史召入，王叔文與準有舊，引用為翰林學士，轉員外郎。 坐叔文貶連州。 準有史學，尚古文，撰《邠志》二卷。
In the twentieth year of Zhenyuan, Ling Zhun was summoned from his posts as Zhedong observation aide and attendant censor; Wang Shuwen, who had known him before, brought him in as Hanlin academician and then promoted him to supernumerary official. Implicated in Shuwen's case, he was banished to Lian Prefecture. Zhun was learned in history, favored ancient-style prose, and compiled the Bin Gazetteer in two scrolls.
48
韓泰，貞元中累遷至戶部郎中，王叔文用為範希朝神策行營節度行軍司馬。 泰最有籌畫，能決陰事，深為伾、叔文之所重，坐貶，自虔州司馬量移漳州刺史，遷郴州。
During Zhenyuan, Han Tai rose repeatedly to Director of the Ministry of Revenue; Wang Shuwen appointed him military aide to Fan Xichao, commander of the Shence expeditionary forces. Tai was the best planner among them and could settle secret matters; Pi and Shuwen relied on him heavily. After banishment he was transferred by measure from aide of Qian to prefect of Zhang, then moved to Chen.
49
柳宗元、劉禹錫自有傳。
Liu Zongyuan and Liu Yuxi have their own biographies.
50
程异，京兆長安人。 嘗侍父疾，鄉里以孝悌稱。 明經及第，釋褐揚州海陵主簿。 登《開元禮》科，授華州鄭縣尉。 精於吏職，剖判無滯。 杜確刺同州，帥河中，皆從為賓佐。
Cheng Yi was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao. He once nursed his father through illness and was praised in his home district for filial devotion. He passed the classics examination and took his first post as recorder of Hailing in Yang Prefecture. He passed the Kaiyuan Rites examination and was appointed bailiff of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture. He was skilled in administrative work and rendered judgments without delay. When Du Que governed Tong Prefecture and then commanded Hezhong, Yi served as his staff aide in both posts.
51
貞元末，擢授監察御史，遷虞部員外郎，充鹽鐵轉運、揚子院留後。 時王叔文用事，由逕放利者皆附之，异亦被引用。 叔文敗，坐貶岳州刺史，改郴州司馬。 元和初，鹽鐵使李巽薦異曉達錢穀，請棄瑕錄用，擢為侍御史，復為揚子留後，累檢校兵部郎中、淮南等五道兩稅使。 异自悔前非，厲己竭節，江淮錢穀之弊，多所鏟革。 入為太府少卿、太卿，轉衛尉卿，兼御史中丞，充鹽鐵轉運副使。
At the end of Zhenyuan he was promoted to investigating censor, then Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, and acting salt and iron transport commissioner and Yangzi depot superintendent. At that time Wang Shuwen held power; everyone who profited by irregular means attached himself to Shuwen, and Yi too was brought into service. After Shuwen's fall he was implicated and demoted to prefect of Yue, then reassigned as aide of Chen. At the beginning of Yuanhe, salt commissioner Li Xun recommended Yi as expert in currency and grain accounts and asked that his faults be overlooked; he was promoted to attendant censor, again made Yangzi depot superintendent, and successively made acting Director of the Ministry of War and dual-tax commissioner for the five Huainan circuits. Yi repented his former errors, disciplined himself, and devoted his integrity; he reformed many abuses in Jianghuai currency and grain. He entered service as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then Director, then Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, and deputy salt and iron transport commissioner.
52
時淮西用兵，國用不足，异使江表以調征賦，且諷有土者以饒羨入貢，至則不剝下，不浚財，經費以贏，人頗便之。 由是專領鹽鐵轉運使、兼御史大夫。 十三年九月，轉工部侍郎、同中書門下平章事，領使如故。 議者以異起錢穀吏，一旦位冠百僚，人情大為不可。 異自知叨據，以謙遜自牧，月餘日，不敢知印秉筆。 异知西北邊軍政不理，建議置巡邊使，上問誰可使者，异請自行。 議未決，無疾而卒，元和十四年四月也。 贈左僕射，謚曰恭。 异性廉約，歿官第，家無餘財，人士多之。
At that time troops were deployed in Huai-Xi and state revenue was insufficient; Yi went to the lower Yangzi to adjust tax levies and urged landowners to contribute surplus wealth as tribute. When he arrived he did not strip the common people or drain wealth; expenses were met with surplus, and the people found it convenient. From this he was given sole charge as salt and iron transport commissioner, Concurrent Censor-in-Chief. In the ninth month of the thirteenth year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works and Regular Second-Rank Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, retaining his commission as before. Commentators held that Yi had risen from a grain-and-currency clerk to rank above the hundred officials overnight; public sentiment found this deeply unacceptable. Knowing he had received an unmerited post, Yi cultivated humility; for more than a month he dared not handle the seal or wield the brush. Yi knew military administration on the northwestern frontier was in disorder and proposed establishing frontier inspection commissioners; when the emperor asked who could be sent, Yi volunteered to go himself. Before the proposal was decided he died without illness, in the fourth month of the fourteenth year of Yuanhe. He was posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous title Gong. Yi's nature was frugal and restrained; he died in his official residence with no surplus wealth, and men of standing praised him.
53
皇甫鎛，安定朝那人。 祖鄰幾，汝州刺史。 父愉，常州刺史。 鎛貞元初登進士第，登賢良文學制科，授監察御史。 丁母憂，免喪，坐居喪時薄遊，除詹事府司直。 轉吏部員外郎、判南曹，凡三年，頗鈐制奸吏。 改吏部郎中，三遷司農卿、兼御史中丞，賜金紫，判度支，俄拜戶部侍郎。 時方討淮西，切於饋運，鎛勾剝嚴急，儲供辦集，益承寵遇，加兼御史大夫。
Huangfu Bo was a native of Chaona in Ding Prefecture. His grandfather Linji was prefect of Ru Prefecture. His father Yu was prefect of Chang Prefecture. Bo at the beginning of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi examination and the special examination in worthy and cultivated literary composition, and was appointed investigating censor. When his mother died he left office for mourning; after mourning ended he was punished for light travel during mourning and was appointed aide of straight conduct in the Heir Apparent's household. He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and controller of the Southern Bureau; for three years in all he kept corrupt clerks firmly in check. He was changed to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, promoted three times to Director of the Court of Imperial Granaries, Concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief, granted the gold seal and purple ribbon, and given charge of the Department of Public Works; soon he was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue. At that time the Huai-Xi campaign was underway and supply transport was urgent; Bo's exactions were severe and strict, stores were assembled, and his favor increased; he was additionally made Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
54
十三年，與鹽鐵使程异同日以本官同平章事，領使如故。 鎛雖有吏才，素無公望，特以聚斂媚上，刻削希恩。 詔書既下，物情駭異，至於賈販無識，亦相嗤誚。 宰相崔群、裴度以物議上聞，憲宗怒而不聽。 度上疏乞罷知政事，因論之曰：
In the thirteenth year he and salt commissioner Cheng Yi were on the same day made Regular Second-Rank Counselors in their existing offices, retaining their commissions as before. Though Bo had administrative talent, he had never enjoyed public esteem; he relied solely on amassing revenue to flatter the emperor and on harsh exactions to seek favor. Once the edict was issued, public sentiment was shocked and dismayed; even ignorant peddlers joined in ridicule. Chancellors Cui Qun and Pei Du reported public opinion to the throne; Emperor Xianzong was angry and would not listen. Pei Du submitted a memorial requesting to be relieved of his duties in governance, and in the course of argument wrote:
55
伏以陛下睿哲文明，唯在所授，凡所閱視，洞達無遺。 所以比來選任宰相，縱道不周物，才不濟時，公望所歸，皆有可取。 況皇甫鎛自掌財賦，唯事割剝，以苛為察，以刻為明。 自京北、京西城鎮及百司並遠近州府，應是仰給度支之處，無不苦口切齒，願食其肉； 猶賴臣等每加勸誡，或為奏論，庶事之中，抑令通濟。 比者淮西諸軍糧料，所破五成錢，其實只與一成、兩成，士卒怨怒，皆欲離叛。 臣到行營，方且慰喻，直其遷延不進，供軍漸難，俱能前行，必有優賞，以此約定，然後切勒供軍官，且支九月一日兩成已上錢，俱容努力，方將小安，不然必有潰散。 今舊兵悉向淄青討伐，忽聞此人入相，則必相與驚擾，以為更有前時之事，則無告訴之憂。 雖侵刻不少，然漏落亦多，所以罷兵之後，經費錢數一千三十萬貫，此事猶可。 直以性惟狡詐，言不誠實，朝三暮四，天下共知，惟能上惑聖聰，足見奸邪之極。 程异雖人品凡俗，然心事和平，處之煩劇，或亦得力，但升之相位，便在公卿之上，實亦非宜。 如皇甫镈，天下之人，怨入骨髓，陛下今日收為股肱，列在臺鼎，切恐不可，伏惟圖之。 倘陛下納臣懇款，速賜移易，以副天下之望，則天下幸甚。 伏聞李翛疾病，亦求入來，如浙西觀察使，且與亦得。
I respectfully submit that Your Majesty is wise, perceptive, and cultivated in the arts; whatever you appoint, whatever you examine, you see through completely without omission. Therefore in recent selections of chancellors, even when conduct did not embrace all things or talent did not meet the needs of the times, those in whom public esteem converged all had something to commend them. Moreover, since Huangfu Bo took charge of fiscal affairs, he has devoted himself only to extortion—taking harshness for discernment and severity for clarity. From the garrisons north and west of the capital and from the hundred offices to distant and nearby prefectures—every place that depends on supplies from the Department of Public Works—none fail to gnash their teeth in bitterness and wish to eat his flesh; we have still had to admonish and counsel repeatedly, or memorialize on their behalf, restraining matters so that supplies could get through. Recently the grain funds of the Huai-Xi armies were supposed to be disbursed at fifty percent, but in fact only ten or twenty percent were given; the soldiers were resentful and angry and all wished to desert. When I reached the expeditionary camp I was just comforting and instructing them; I excused their delay in advancing, explained that supply was growing difficult, promised generous rewards if they all advanced, and on that basis made an agreement; then I strictly ordered the supply officers to disburse at least twenty percent of the funds due on the first day of the ninth month, so that with effort they might find some relief—otherwise there would certainly be collapse and dispersal. Now the veteran troops are all marching to campaign against Ziqing; if they suddenly hear this man has entered the chancellorship, they will surely be alarmed together, thinking there will be more of what happened before—then there will be no recourse for their complaints. Though his exactions were considerable, his leakages were also great; thus after the troops were disbanded there remained 10.3 million strings of cash in expenses—this matter is still tolerable. It is simply that his nature is solely crafty and deceitful, his words insincere—changing morning and evening, known to all under Heaven; that he can only delude the sacred understanding shows the extreme of wickedness. Though Cheng Yi is vulgar in character, his mind is peaceful, and in handling demanding affairs he may prove useful; but to raise him to the chancellorship, placing him above the highest nobles, is truly also inappropriate. As for Huangfu Bo—the people of the realm hate him to the marrow; if Your Majesty today takes him as your arm and leg and seats him among the highest ministers, I fear deeply this cannot be done—I beg Your Majesty to consider it. If Your Majesty accepts my earnest plea and promptly grants a change, fulfilling the hopes of all under Heaven, then the realm will be greatly blessed. I have heard that Li Xiao is ill and also seeks to return from his post; appointment as Zhexi observation commissioner, or the like, would also be acceptable.
56
臣知一言出口，必犯天威，但使言行，甘心獲戾。 今者臣若不退，天下之人謂臣有負恩寵； 今退毀未許，言又不聽，如火燒心，若箭攢體。 臣自無足惜，惜陛下今日事勢。 何者？ 淮西蕩定，河北咸寧，承宗斂手削地，程權束身赴闕，韓弘輿疾討賊，此豈京師氣力能制其命，祗是朝廷處置能服其心。 今既開中興，再造區夏，陛下何忍卻自破除，使億萬之眾離心，四方諸侯解體？ 凡百君子，皆欲慟哭。 況陛下任臣之意，豈比常人； 臣事陛下之心，敢同眾士？ 所以昧死重封以聞，如不足觀，臣當引領受責。 陛下引一市肆商徒，與臣同列，在臣亦有何損，陛下實有所傷，不勝憤懣惶恐之至。
I know that one word from my mouth will surely offend celestial wrath, but so long as my words match my deeds, I willingly accept punishment. If I do not withdraw now, the people of the realm will say I have betrayed Your Majesty's grace and favor; yet withdrawal is not permitted and my words are not heeded—it is like fire burning my heart, like arrows piercing my body. I myself am not worth regretting; what I regret is Your Majesty's present situation. Why is this? Huai-Xi has been pacified, Hebei is at peace, Chengzong has submitted and surrendered territory, Cheng Quan has bound himself and come to court, and Han Hong, though ill, has campaigned against the rebels—this is not because the capital's strength alone could command their lives, but because the court's handling could win their hearts. Now that restoration has begun and the realm is being rebuilt, how can Your Majesty bear to destroy it yourself, causing hundreds of millions to lose heart and the lords of the four quarters to disintegrate? All the gentlemen wish to weep in anguish. Moreover, the trust Your Majesty places in me—is it comparable to that of ordinary men? The devotion with which I serve Your Majesty—dare I be the same as the multitude? Therefore I risk death to seal this again and report it; if it is not worth considering, I shall stretch my neck to accept punishment. Your Majesty has brought in a marketplace peddler to rank with me—what loss is that to me? But Your Majesty will truly be harmed. I am overwhelmed with indignation, distress, and dread beyond bearing.
57
時憲宗以世道漸平，欲肆意娛樂，池臺館宇，稍增崇飾，而异、鎛探知上旨，數貢羨餘，以備經構，故帝獨排物議相之； 見裴度疏，以為朋黨，竟不省覽。 鎛知公議不可，益以巧媚自固，奏減內外官俸錢以贍國用； 敕下，給事中崔祐封還詔書，其事方罷。 時內出積年庫物付度支估價，例皆陳朽，鎛盡以善價買之，以給邊軍。 羅縠繒彩，觸風斷裂，隨手散壞，軍士怨怒，皆聚而焚之。 裴度奏事，因言邊軍焚賜之意，鎛因引其足奏曰：「此靴乃內庫出者，臣以俸二千買之，堅韌可以久服，所言不可用，皆詐也。」 帝以為然，由是鎛益無忌憚。 裴度有用兵伐叛之功，鎛心嫉之，與宰相李逢吉、令狐楚合勢擠度出鎮太原。 崔群有公望，為搢紳所重，屢言時政之弊，鎛惡之，因議憲宗尊號，乃奏曰：「昨群臣議上徽號，崔群於陛下惜『孝德』兩字。」 憲宗怒，黜群為湖南觀察使。 又與金吾將軍李道古恊為奸謀，薦引方士柳泌、僧大通，言可致長生。 中尉吐突承璀恩寵莫二，鎛厚賂結其歡心，故及相位。
At that time Emperor Xianzong, believing the age was growing peaceful, wished to indulge freely in pleasure; pools, terraces, and halls were gradually made more splendid, and Yi and Bo, discerning the emperor's intent, repeatedly presented surplus revenue to supply construction—therefore the emperor alone overrode public opinion to make them chancellors; when he saw Pei Du's memorial he took it for factionalism and would not read it at all. Bo knew public opinion could not be withstood and all the more used clever flattery to secure himself; he memorialized to reduce the salary payments of inner and outer officials to supply state expenses; once the edict was issued, Supervising Secretary Cui You returned the edict unapproved, and the matter was then dropped. At that time stored goods from years past in the inner treasury were handed to the Department of Public Works for valuation; by rule they were all decayed and worn, yet Bo bought them all at good prices to supply the border armies. Silks and brocades snapped and tore at a touch and fell apart in the hand; the soldiers were resentful and angry and all gathered to burn them. Pei Du was reporting on affairs and spoke of the border troops' burning of gifts; Huangfu Bo then drew up his foot and memorialized, "These boots came from the inner treasury; I bought them for two thousand strings of my salary—they are sturdy and durable for long wear. What has been said about their uselessness is all fraud." The emperor thought this correct, and from this Bo became all the more unbridled. Pei Du had merit in campaigning against rebellion; Bo resented him in his heart and, with chancellors Li Fengji and Linghu Chu, combined forces to force Du out to command Taiyuan. Cui Qun enjoyed public esteem and was respected by the gentry; he repeatedly spoke of abuses in current policy, and Bo hated him; on the occasion of deliberating Emperor Xianzong's honorific title he memorialized, "When the officials recently deliberated the honorific title, Cui Qun begrudged Your Majesty the two characters 'Filial' and 'Virtuous.'" Emperor Xianzong was angry and demoted Qun to Zhexi observation commissioner. He also joined with Gold Crowns General Li Daogu in wicked plotting, recommending and bringing in the adept Liu Bi and the monk Datong, saying they could bring long life. Chief Palace Intendant Tuchi Chenghui enjoyed favor without rival; Bo lavished bribes to win his goodwill, and thus reached the chancellorship.
58
穆宗在東宮，備聞鎛之奸邪，及居諒闇，聽政之日，詔：「皇甫鎛器本凡近，性惟險狹，行靡所顧，文無可觀，雖早踐朝倫，而素乖公望。 自掌邦計，屬當軍興，以剝下為徇公，既鼓眾怒； 以矯跡為孤立，用塞人言。 洎塵臺司，益蠹時政，不知經國之大體，不慮安邊之遠圖，三軍多凍餒之憂，百姓深雕瘵之弊。 事皆罔蔽，言悉虛誣，遠近咸知，朝野同怨。 而又恣求方士，上惑先朝，潛通奸人，罪在難舍。 合加竄殛，以正刑章，俾黜遐荒，尚存寬典。」 又詔曰：「山人柳泌輒懷左道，上惑先朝，固求牧人，貴欲疑眾，自知虛誕，仍便奔逃。 僧大通醫方不精，藥術皆妄。 既延禍釁，俱是奸邪，邦國固有常刑，人神所宜共棄，宜付京兆府決重杖一頓處死。」
Muzong, while heir apparent, had fully heard of Bo's wickedness; on the day he assumed mourning and began to govern, an edict read, "Huangfu Bo's capacity is fundamentally commonplace, his nature solely treacherous and narrow, his conduct heedless of consequences, his writing unworthy of note; though he long trod the court ranks, he had always fallen short of public esteem. Once he took charge of state finance, at a time of military mobilization, he made stripping the people below his public service and thereby roused the anger of the masses; he used affected conduct to pose as isolated, thereby silencing men's words. When he reached the censorate he further corrupted current policy, ignorant of the great principles of governing the state and heedless of the far-reaching plan of securing the borders; the three armies suffered much from cold and hunger, and the common people bore deep wounds of ruin. His affairs were all concealed and deceived, his words entirely false; near and far alike knew it, court and countryside shared the resentment. Moreover he recklessly sought out adepts, deluding the former emperor, and secretly communicated with wicked men—crimes that cannot be pardoned. He should be further banished and executed to rectify the penal code; yet demotion to remote exile still preserves the lenient statute." Another edict read, "The mountain man Liu Bi presumptuously harbored heterodox ways, deluding the former emperor; he insisted on governing the people, clearly intending to deceive the multitude; knowing his own fraud, he then fled. The monk Datong was unskilled in medical formulas; his drug arts were all false. Having brought calamity and offense, both are wicked men; the state has its regular punishments, and gods and men alike should cast them out—let the metropolitan prefecture decide: heavy beating once, then execution."
59
柳泌本曰楊仁力，少習醫術，言多誕妄。 李道古奸回巧宦，與泌密謀求進，言之於皇甫镈，因征入禁中。 自雲能致靈藥，言：「天臺山多靈草，君仙所會，臣嘗知之，而力不能致。 願為天臺長吏，因以求之。」 起徒步為臺州刺史，仍賜金紫。 諫官論奏曰：「列聖亦有好方士者，亦與官號，未嘗令賦政臨民。」 憲宗曰：「煩一郡之力而致神仙長年，臣子於君父何愛焉！」 由是莫取有言者。 裴潾以極言被黜。 泌到天臺，驅役吏民於山谷間，聲言采藥，鞭笞躁急。 歲余一無所得，懼詐發獲罪，舉家入山谷。 浙東觀察使追捕，送於京師，镈與李道古懇保證之，必能可致靈藥，乃待詔翰林院。 憲宗服泌藥，日益煩躁，喜怒不常，內官懼非罪見戮，遂為弒逆。 大通自雲壽一百五十歲，久得藥力。 又有田佐元者，鳳翔虢人，自言有奇術，能變瓦礫為金，白衣授虢縣令。 初，柳泌系京兆府，獄吏叱之曰：「何苦作此虛矯？」 泌曰：「吾本無此心，是李道古教我，且雲壽四百歲。」 府吏防虞周密，恐其隱化； 及解衣就誅，一無變異，但灸灼之瘢痕浹身而已。 镈卒於貶所。
Liu Bi was originally named Yang Renli; in youth he studied medicine and his words were mostly wild and false. Li Daogu was a treacherous and crafty official; he plotted secretly with Bi to seek advancement and spoke of him to Huangfu Bo, who then summoned him into the inner palace. He claimed he could obtain elixir drugs and said, "Mount Tiantai has many spirit herbs and is where immortals gather; I have known this, but my strength could not obtain them. I wish to become prefect of Tiantai and thereby seek them." He was raised from commoner to prefect of Tai Prefecture and also granted the gold seal and purple ribbon. Remonstrating officials memorialized, "The successive sage emperors also had adepts they favored and gave them titles, but they never let them govern and face the people." Emperor Xianzong said, "What is troubling one prefecture's resources to obtain immortality and long life—what would a subject withhold from his lord and father!" From this no one dared speak further. Pei Zuan was demoted for speaking to the limit. When Bi reached Tiantai he drove officials and commoners in the mountain valleys, claiming to gather herbs, with urgent beatings. After more than a year he obtained nothing; fearing exposure of his fraud and punishment, he took his whole family into the mountains. The Zhedong observation commissioner pursued and sent him to the capital; Bo and Li Daogu earnestly guaranteed that he could certainly obtain elixir drugs, and so he awaited orders in the Hanlin Academy. Emperor Xianzong took Bi's drugs and grew daily more restless; his joy and anger were irregular, and inner attendants feared being killed without cause and then committed regicide. Datong claimed for himself a lifespan of one hundred fifty years and long enjoyment of the drug's power. There was also Tian Zuoyuan, a native of Guo in Fengxiang, who claimed strange arts and could transform rubble into gold; in commoner's dress he was appointed magistrate of Guo County. At first Liu Bi was held in the metropolitan prefecture prison; the jailer rebuked him, "Why go to such trouble with this empty pretense?" Liu Bi said, "I never had this intention—it was Li Daogu who taught me, and he claimed I would live four hundred years." The prefectural officers guarded him with meticulous care, fearing he might vanish by transformation; when he stripped for execution there was no transformation at all—only the burn scars from cauterization covered his body. Bo died in his place of banishment.
60
镈弟鏞，端士也。 亦進士擢第，累歷宣歙、鳳翔使府從事，入為殿中侍御史，轉比部員外郎、河南縣令、都官郎中、河南少尹。 時镈為宰相，領度支，恩寵殊異。 鏞惡其太盛，每弟兄宴語，即極言之，镈頗不悅。 乃求為分司，除右庶子。 及镈獲罪，朝廷素知鏞有先見之明，不之罪，征為國子祭酒，改太子賓客、秘書監。 開成初，除太子少保分司，卒年四十九。 鏞能文，尤工詩什，樂道自怡，不屑世務，當時名士皆與之交。 有集十八卷，著《性言》十四篇。
Bo's younger brother Yong was an upright gentleman. He too passed the jinshi examination, served successively as staff member in the Xuanchen and Fengxiang commissionerates, entered service as attendant censor within the palace, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue, magistrate of Henan County, Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and Vice Governor of Henan. At that time Bo was chancellor and in charge of the Department of Public Works, enjoying extraordinary favor. Yong hated his excessive power; whenever the brothers feasted and talked together he spoke against it to the utmost, and Bo was quite displeased. He then requested a detached-office post and was appointed Right Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's household. When Bo was punished, the court had long known Yong had foresight and did not punish him; he was summoned as Director of the Directorate of Education, then changed to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Director of the Secretariat. At the beginning of Kaicheng he was appointed Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent in detached office and died at age forty-nine. Yong could write, was especially skilled in poetry, delighted in the Way and found joy in himself, disdained worldly affairs, and the celebrated men of the time all associated with him. He left a collection in eighteen scrolls and composed Fourteen Chapters on Nature.
61
【贊】=史臣曰：奸邪害正，自古有之； 而矯誕無忌，妒賢傷善，未有如延齡、皇甫之甚也。 臣每讀陸丞相論延齡疏，未嘗不泣下沾衿，其守正效忠，為宗社大計，非端士益友，安能感激犯難如此？ 異哉德宗之為人主也，忠良不用，讒慝是崇，乃至身播國屯，幾將覆滅，尚獨保延齡之是，不悟盧杞之非，悲夫！ 執誼、叔文，乘時多僻，而欲斡運六合，斟酌萬幾； 劉、柳諸生，逐臭市利，何狂妄之甚也！ 章武雄材睿斷，翦削厲階； 洎逐群、度而相異、镈，蓋季年之妖惑也，夫何言哉！
[Praise] The chronicler states: Wicked men harming the upright has existed since antiquity; yet feigned extravagance without restraint, envying talent and harming the good—none have been as extreme as Yanling and Huangfu Bo. Whenever I read Chancellor Lu's memorial against Yanling, I never fail to weep until my collar is wet; his upholding rectitude and loyal service for the great plan of the altars of soil and grain—without an upright gentleman and good friend, who could be stirred to brave difficulty like this? How strange that Dezong as lord was such: the loyal and good he would not employ, slanderers he exalted—until he himself was driven abroad and the state brought to near ruin, yet he still upheld Yanling as right and did not perceive Lu Qi's wrong. Pitiful! Wei Zhiyi and Wang Shuwen, seizing an irregular time with many perversities, yet wished to turn the six directions and weigh the myriad affairs of state; Liu Yuxi, Liu Zongyuan, and the other scholars, chasing stench for market profit—how extreme their arrogance! Zhangwu had heroic talent and keen judgment, cutting away dangerous steps; yet when he expelled Qun and Du and made Yi and Bo chancellors, that was the bewitchment of his late years—what more is there to say!
62
贊曰：貞元之風，好佞惡忠。 齡、镈害善，為國蠹蟲。 裴、陸獻替，嫉惡如風。 天聽匪諶，吾道斯窮。
The praise reads: The wind of Zhenyuan favored flatterers and hated the loyal. Yanling and Bo harmed the good and were worms devouring the state. Pei and Lu offered correction, hating evil like a gale. Heaven's hearing was not true; our Way was thus at an end.
